items.q: What's wrong with trusting SWE Bench headlines?
items.a: Labs are **bench-maxing** — training for SWE Bench Pro / Verified scores while real output diverges. Public posts drive impressions; **output quality > leaderboard rank** for vibe coding decisions.

items.q: Did Kimi K2.6 get the BridgeMind stamp?
items.a: **No** — won't use it personally despite marketing parity vs GPT 5.4 Extra High / Opus 4.6 / Gemini 3.1 Pro. Leading open-source ≠ frontier closed for shipping UI.

items.q: What are K2.6's size, context, and price?
items.a: **1.1T parameters**, **595 GB** on Hugging Face (not consumer-runnable); **262K** context; ~**$0.95/M** in, **$4/M** out via Moonshot API or OpenRouter. Open-weight but best accessed via API.

items.q: What does Agent Swarm (beta) actually do?
items.a: Creates **named role subagents** (e.g. asset gen "Shannon", engine "Woo") that collaborate on a TypeScript zombies game (~**30–60 min**). Swarm builds **complete apps** even when prompted for a single HTML file — but game output was poor (zombie count mismatch, decorative beams).

items.q: Where does K2.6 shine on BridgeBench?
items.a: **#5 overall** (up from K2.5 at #17); standout **#1 debugging** (beats Opus 4.6/4.7, GPT 5.4); **#3 hallucination**, **#4 refactoring**; ~**95 tok/s**.

items.q: Where does UI and game output fail?
items.a: Lava Lamp added **unrequested** speed/glow/color controls; Snake/Flappy/Breakout failed. Website revamp: broken light/dark, **random rising white block** on pricing; single agent unfinished in **14 min** vs Opus 4.7 polish.
Adding features **not in the prompt** (Lava Lamp controls) is scary in a NestJS API context. Same jagged pattern: elite debugging + failed games/UI in one model.

items.q: What credit does Moonshot still get?
items.a: Probably the **leading open-source coding model** with a massive **K2.5 → K2.6** BridgeBench jump — just **cannot compare to frontier closed models** for production UI/shipping.
